Nvidia shares fall more than 5% as Huang comeback rally cools

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (593 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia shares fell 5.86% on Tuesday, paring a massive Monday rally that was sparked by the return of Jensen Huang as CEO.
  • semiconductor stocks also traded lower after posting strong increases Monday.
  • Neoclouds gave back some of their Monday gains, with CoreWeave losing 11.84%, Iren declining 11.54% and Nebius shedding 10.74%.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia shares fell 5.86% on Tuesday, paring a massive Monday rally that was sparked by the return of Jensen Huang as CEO.

Other U.S. semiconductor stocks also traded lower after posting strong increases Monday. Micron declined 10.97%, Marvell Technology lost 9.10%, Arm Holdings dropped 8.55% and AMD shed 8.86%.

Neoclouds gave back some of their Monday gains, with CoreWeave losing 11.84%, Iren declining 11.54% and Nebius shedding 10.74%.

Recent findings suggest that huang, who resigned as CEO of Nvidia earlier this month after admitting to an extramarital affair, was reinstated on Monday. The stock closed over 30% higher following the news of Huang's return.

The company's board of directors stated it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him.

President Donald Trump also claimed he was personally involved in Huang's return. The president told CNBC that he spoke with the chipmaker's board before it reversed course and reinstated its co-founder.

"I made the deal," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers on Monday during an interview on "Squawk on the Street.".

Trump remarked Nvidia's board asked for guarantees that Huang, who resigned less than two weeks ago, was not a threat to national security.

"And we gave them assurances, at least with everything we know," the president stated. "We believe he's fine. He's absolutely fine.".

Many Nvidia employees welcomed Huang's reinstatement, with multiple floors of employees greeting the CEO with cheers Monday at Nvidia's headquarters. In an employee meeting Tuesday, Huang struck a somber tone and acknowledged the impact of his actions. In the first such meeting since his return, Huang doubled down on his stance regarding succession planning, saying Nvidia's unique business model doesn't require it, according to people inside the room.

After Huang's reinstatement, several Wall Street analysts turned more bullish on the stock and upgraded their ratings on Nvidia.

"We believe reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang RETURNS Investor CONFIDENCE in the AI trade," Mizuho analysts wrote in a note on Monday.

Huang and Nvidia have been central to the AI story, supplying the chips that power AI and financing companies across the ecosystem.

The tech giant remains under scrutiny as questions remain about Huang's reported affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy.

Industry observers note that the U.S. is investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed, the company where she worked. Questions also remain regarding whether Nvidia chips are making their way into China despite export controls.

Huang is set to publicly testify in front of the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, who is set to take over the Committee in January, called Huang's reinstatement "reckless.".

Sources indicate that "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the manufacturer's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Warren said in a statement on Monday.

It has been revealed that huang is also expected to sit for a closed-door interview with the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select committees on Dec. 1. The hearing falls on the same day Huang, before his resignation, was scheduled to give the keynote address at Nvidia's annual GTC conference in Washington, D.C.

"Reinstatement should not be confused with the end of scrutiny," Bank of America said in a note on Monday. "We therefore expect elevated attention around governance, China/export controls, customer relationships and compliance to persist even with the CEO question resolved.".

— CNBC's Luke Fountain, Seema Mody and Dan Mangan contributed to this report.

    #188076. Does the Nvidia-led rip mark the market bottom? Maybe not

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1472 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Does the Nvidia-led rip mark the market bottom? Maybe not

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1472 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the key accelerant to Monday's ripping rebound was a shocker.
    • The S&P 500's 4.7% surge on Monday lifted it out of a steep-sided hole following last week's washout selling storm.
    • In a recent development, more than a third of the S&P's gain was provided by the 31% jump in Nvidia shares alone following Jensen Huang's stunning reinstatement as Nvidia CEO.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the key accelerant to Monday's ripping rebound was a shocker. But the level that halted the rally was right where you'd expect.

    The S&P 500's 4.7% surge on Monday lifted it out of a steep-sided hole following last week's washout selling storm. Its high for the day was just under 7300, a level last seen on Thursday, corresponding to the index's summertime low and representing the floor of the former multi-month trading range. In other words, the pop stopped at the point from which the tape had broken down; the index slipped three-quarters of a percent from there by the close.

    In a recent development, more than a third of the S&P's gain was provided by the 31% jump in Nvidia shares alone following Jensen Huang's stunning reinstatement as Nvidia CEO. Here, too, the stock closed right near the Iran-selloff low, which it cracked through some 12 days ago. It remains under all the relevant moving averages and trend lines.

    This isn't to minimize or denigrate these moves of rare magnitude, but simply to place them in context. The market was going to attempt a solid bounce no matter the news. S&P 500 futures were indicated higher by more than 2% even before the Huang bombshell struck before Monday's open.

    According to recent reports, by near-universal agreement, last week's flush had generated the kind of indiscriminate liquidation, oversold conditions and urgent hedging that typically set up at least a snapback rip. Some of these readings were as extreme as near the April 2025 low following the tariff panic, though not all.

    Sources indicate that the reinstallation of Huang at the apparent behest of the White House triggered an emotional, spring-loaded ramp in the AI trade, a collective panic by the under-invested. When the government jolts the market with a policy shift like this, it not only assuages a prevailing fear in the market, but it grants psychic permission to investors who were frantically selling one day to ravenously buy back the same stocks the next.

    It's slightly ironic, given that a common line last week on the recent market setback was that – unlike in the tariff panic or the Iran war corrections – there was no single policy reversal that could short-circuit the selloff and trigger a ferocious recovery.

    It has been revealed that and maybe there still isn't. Such one-day comebacks from a deeply oversold state are to be respected but not fully trusted. Looking back at prior one-day gains of such amplitude – or prior sequences of a daily drop and gain of more than 5% in the Nasdaq-100 – generate a fair number of episodes inside of nasty bear markets, along with a few consequential market bottoms.

    A few further observations and questions at a potentially tenuous tactical moment for the markets:.

    Sources indicate that -The standard playbook is to assume that we've put in "a low, not the final low." Oversold rallies can carry on a while – say, to the 20-day moving average, which for the S&P 500 is up another 3% from here – without getting escape velocity. Graybeards argue for keeping the market on a short leash, expecting there will at least be a retest sequence. Prudent to assume so, though it's inescapable that V-shaped bottoms have become a bit more common in recent years, as recently as at the end of March, on the merest hint that President Trump would consider ceasing Iran hostilities without forcing open the Strait of Hormuz.

    Industry observers note that -Index corrections of at least 10% that happen quickly have generally been more associated with temporary bull-market dips than the start of nastier downturns. This latest S&P 500 correction happened over 33 trading days, among the dozen quickest. That would be reassuring, except that places it right between the declines of November 2007 and February 2022, which indeed were the start of bear markets.

    Recent findings suggest that -Remember that the pain of this setback was inflicted after months in which Wall Street was constantly extolling the virtues of a "broadening" market (equal-weight S&P 500 outperforming) and marveling at the elegant rotation into "quality" and defensive stocks that was supporting the S&P 500. Those mechanics can work fine in phases, but never allow for a proper market-wide reset and, clearly, they don't inoculate the tape from eventual washouts.

    Industry observers note that -We might have a new binary trading relationship to watch: It's early in the game, but with the Nvidia news jolting most AI plays higher, Anthropic in its third trading session since its IPO fell 1.4%. If Nvidia is an advocate for and backer of global open-weight models, then its revival could dim the view of Anthropic's closed frontier AI platform, while diminishing the advantage provided by Anthropic's $200 billion cash capex war chest.

    In a recent development, john Kolovos of Macro Risk Advisors on the latest reading: "The growing evidence of capitulation is encouraging. Bearish sentiment was arguably the market's best attribute coming into last week and still is. Sentiment became even more extreme over the past week, pushing our model to its lowest reading since the 2025 bottom, and reaching levels comparable to what we saw during the 2022 bear market. The six-month outlook has improved, but whether this is a V bottom thanks to the return of Jensen Huang, or the market undergoes basing and a possible retest, remains unclear.".

    -I'm making my way through "The AGI Chronicles: The Inside Story of the Race to Create an Artificial Superintelligence," the new book by former New York Times technology writer Kevin Roose, a smart, engaging and brisk history of AI development and the personalities driving it. For a shortcut through the material, Roose's discussion on the New Yorker Radio Hour podcast is worth a listen.

    -In returning to Nvidia headquarters Monday without his signature leather jacket, Jensen Huang was executing a Reverse Fonzie.

    In the first season of "Happy Days," the mega-hit sitcom of the '70s and early '80s, ABC forced the Fonz character to wear a cloth windbreaker, fearing he'd alienate viewers who'd take him for a "hoodlum." Creator Garry Marshall argued to the network that a leather jacket was a safety requirement for motorcycle riders and pushed to let him wear. When the show took off, the leather became standard.

    Huang is now perhaps trying to seem a bit less edgy, humble and relatable absent the biker attire.

    President Trump's direct intervention to press Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang, juicing the Nasdaq for at least a day, reintroduced investors to the notion that stocks can only fall so far without the administration trying to punish the sellers.

    Recent findings suggest that but can Wall Street enjoy both a Trump put and a Fed put? If conviction about the AI trade and its aggressive spending is revived, and the economy runs hotter, and private-sector borrowing rises, will that not invite a more hawkish Federal Reserve – at just the time that many were handicapping a dovish pivot given the unsettled markets of late?

    According to recent reports, it's a live question. More than a month ago, as a fourth-quarter post-election rally was becoming consensus, I granted the setup but with a key caveat:.

    It has been revealed that "Still, against most probabilities, 2018 happened. By which I mean a 19% S&P 500 peak-to-trough decline in the fourth quarter of a midterm-election year, one that saw total S&P 500 earnings grow by more than 20%. The 2018 tailspin had followed a massive momentum crescendo and reversal several months earlier, which gave way to an erratic tape that couldn't absorb what seemed at the time relatively unthreatening Federal Reserve tightening actions.".

    Since then, after the market retrenchment, the 2018 analogy has grown so popular that I doubt it will unfold exactly that way. Still, as Renaissance Macro noted after Monday's rally, Nvidia's gain, which helped the S&P 500 recoup half of last week's loss, "may have fixed the S&P 500 loss but not the Fed, the [Treasury] curve or cash credit.".

    Higher real yields remain a potential constraint on equity valuations. This chart from Wellington Management reveals the yield on 30-year Treasury Inflation Protected Securities – the long-term real yield – is now above the S&P 500's free-cash-flow yield for the first time in half a generation.

    It has been revealed that in a related vein, JPMorgan economist Bruce Kasman in his 2027 outlook describes a certain narrative dissonance: "Financial markets have projected strong earnings expectations, in part, because central banks have preached immaculate disinflation and been supportive of easy access to credit. The 2027 landscape — of above-potential growth, a sixth year of elevated inflation, and a renewed labor market tightening — poses a meaningful challenge to the magical thinking held by markets and central banks.".

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (575 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Ex-49er Brandon Aiyuk will visit with Commanders after clearing waivers

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (575 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Brandon Aiyuk might have a new home sooner than later.
    • In a recent development, the former 49ers receiver is scheduled to visit with the Washington Commanders.
    • According to recent reports, aiyuk cleared waivers on Tuesday after being released by the 49ers, concluding a protracted and contentious breakup with the franchise.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Brandon Aiyuk might have a new home sooner than later.

    In a recent development, the former 49ers receiver is scheduled to visit with the Washington Commanders. That's according to his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, who told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Aiyuk, 28, will meet with the Commanders on Wednesday.

    According to recent reports, aiyuk cleared waivers on Tuesday after being released by the 49ers, concluding a protracted and contentious breakup with the franchise. The NFL recently reinstated Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list, and the 49ers subsequently cut him.

    The Commanders have had a need at wide receiver virtually all season. No. 1 receiver and former All-Pro Terry McLaurin is on season-ending injured reserve due to a torn patellar tendon in his left knee.

    Recent findings suggest that mcLaurin's injury has pushed offseason acquisition Stefon Diggs to the top of the depth chart alongside rookie Antonio Williams. No other Commanders receiver has more than 16 catches this season.

    According to recent reports, A third-round draft pick, Williams is emerging as a breakout candidate, most notably via his nine-catch, 122-yard performance in Monday's 22-20 upset of the Cincinnati Bengals. Williams made two of those catches for 64 yards in a 46-second drive that set up Drew Stevens' game-winning field goal as time expired.

    Sources indicate that but even with Williams' emergence, the Commanders are thin at the position and kicking the tires on whether Aiyuk can still be a meaningful contributor following a two-year absence from football. They'll also need to evaluate whether they can trust Aiyuk to fill his potential role following his multiyear standoff with the 49ers.

    Can Brandon Aiyuk still be a meaningful NFL contributor?

    Industry observers note that aiyuk sustained a torn ACL and MCL in October 2024, months after signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the 49ers. He failed to report to team facilities in 2025 for his rehabilitation and recovery from those injuries and has not played football since.

    It has been revealed that the result was a dispute over a $13 million roster bonus that the 49ers wanted back because of Aiyuk's refusal to report. The 49ers ultimately declared that he was not welcome back with the franchise.

    Sources indicate that aiyuk has also behaved erratically off the field, including an incident in which he recorded himself speeding past Levi's Stadium at more than 100 mph and posted it on the internet. That ultimately led to a warrant for his arrest.

    It has been revealed that at his best, Aiyuk was an All-Pro contributor on a winning 49ers team. He tallied 75 receptions for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns in 2023 for a team that went to the Super Bowl. That campaign led to his $120 million contract, of which $27 million in guarantees was eventually voided.

    That was three seasons and a serious knee injury ago, in addition to his two years off from football.

    According to recent reports, the Commanders, meanwhile, are in the hunt to win the NFC East following Monday's last-second win over the Bengals. At 4-5-1, they're two games behind a first-place Giants team against which they own the season tiebreaker.

    According to recent reports, if Aiyuk signs with Washington and produces at a portion of the pace he did in 2023, he could be a difference-maker on a team quarterbacked by Jayden Daniels. But the Commanders will have considerably more than Aiyuk's on-field upside to consider before signing him.

    #188066. Tech Report: Commercial real estate activity falls 14% in October, as interest rates rise

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (684 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Commercial real estate activity falls 14% in October, as interest rates rise

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (684 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Interest rates moved higher in September, and that had a swift impact on commercial real estate deal-making.
    • As a result, commercial real estate activity dropped 14% in October from September, according to an index from LightBox, a commercial real estate data platform.
    • The appraisal measure is at its weakest level of the three and is now down 17% from a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Interest rates moved higher in September, and that had a swift impact on commercial real estate deal-making. After settling in the low-to-mid-4% range, the yield on the 10-year Treasury moved above 5% and has been wavering around there with the potential to move even higher due to stubborn inflation.

    As a result, commercial real estate activity dropped 14% in October from September, according to an index from LightBox, a commercial real estate data platform. Of the index's three components, commercial property listings fell 20% from September, environmental site assessments were down 1% and lender appraisals dropped 11%.

    The appraisal measure is at its weakest level of the three and is now down 17% from a year ago. It shows that both lenders and borrowers are stepping back, unable to pencil deals and move from listing to closing.

    Sources indicate that "What makes this so interesting is that during tariffs, it didn't dip. During $100 oil earlier this year, it didn't dip. When we saw interest rates marching up the first half of this year, it didn't dip. In fact, it kind of increased, and now we've fallen off a map in October," noted Manus Clancy, head of data strategy at LightBox. "It's like we've reached this straw that has broken the camel's back in terms of people saying, 'Okay, enough is enough. I can't keep putting money to work without some clarity on where interest rates are going.'".

    In a recent development, clancy said deals were happening earlier this year because investors had gotten more comfortable with where interest rates had settled. The office market was beginning to recover as more companies ordered workers back. Multifamily, which had seen a glut of fresh construction, was also starting to see vacancies fall and rents rise.

    This takes the market back to 2023, when deal-making froze up because interest rates had shot up sharply from very low, pandemic-induced levels. As property values repriced, the gap between what the sellers wanted and what the buyers were willing to pay widened. That is what is happening now.

    "The wheels of progress just completely stop," said Clancy.

    Recent findings suggest that whether they are refinancing a loan or getting a new loan to purchase a property, investors, developers and property owners are now deciding to wait to see if interest rates come down at all. While the Federal Reserve is expected to raise its lending rate further, an end to the war with Iran could bring Treasury yields down. Especially for refinances, borrowers would be out millions of dollars at these higher rates. On the buy side, deals simply don't work anymore at higher rates.

    "I think it is disorienting as people try to rebase values, and in the midst of transactions, you're seeing value retrades at the 11th hour, deals getting pulled, and volume slowing down yet again in the market," said Ryan Cotton, head of real estate at Bain Capital in a recent Property Play podcast. "It's definitely a confusing and complicated time to be a real estate investor.".

    In a recent development, higher interest rates were the leading factor for the slowdown in October, but LightBox cited another contributing factor. Lending remains open, but sentiment has weakened. It points to the Mortgage Bankers Association cutting its 2027 growth forecast for commercial mortgage lending from about 8% to 1%. In addition, the Commercial Real Estate Finance Council, or CREFC, Sentiment Index fell 17.5% in the third quarter of this year to a three-year low.

    It has been revealed that "People are lending for construction. They're lending for office conversion. They're lending for new purchases," noted Clancy. "We look at this index as kind of the tip of the spear. That if something's going to go sideways, this is the first indicator that people are stopping the ordering of appraisals, and we think that this portends that the next quarter will show a lot of decline in bank lending on commercial real estate.".

    CNBC's Property Play with Diana Olick covers latest and evolving opportunities for the real estate investor, delivered weekly to your inbox.

    #188065. Industry News: Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (747 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (747 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S.
    • The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a substantial win for the company and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    According to recent reports, some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    In a recent development, adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and mentioned it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the big indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    It has been revealed that "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he stated.

    Part of the challenge, Niles noted, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," stated JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he stated, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    Sources indicate that anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan stated. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the manufacturer in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he said. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    Industry observers note that one bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.

    Here's a look at the Yahoo Expert League standings after Week 11.

    It was a good week for a few bottom-dwellers in the standings, but let's focus on the top first.

    First-place Hayden Winks was given quite the scare by Ray Garvin in their matchup, before Winks escaped with a 114.06-112.86 victory. Winks entered Monday night trailing in the matchup but with Jayden Daniels and Samaje Perine left to play. The contest was decided on the final drive, when Daniels hit Antonio Williams for back-to-back gains equaling 64 passing yards, enough to push Winks ahead by a hair. It also helped that Perine was able to hit 11.7 fantasy points, thanks mostly to a 4-71-0 receiving line.

    Sources indicate that the win keeps Winks in first place at 8-3 going into Thanksgiving week. The close loss for Garvin could sink his playoff chances with three more matchups to go before the postseason begins in Week 15.

    The other two marquee matchups from Week 11 were Matt Harmon versus Scott Pianowski and Justin Boone versus Eric Edholm, with all four managers entering the week in playoff position.

    Industry observers note that pianowski keeps finding ways to win, and stashing Emmett Johnson has paid off major time for the Yahoo analyst. This matchup was decided on Sunday Night Football with Harmon rostering Kirk Cousins and Pianowski Brock Purdy. The latter was able to post 22.2 points while Cousins only had 8.4. After the loss, Harmon is now at 6-5 and outside the playoff picture in seventh place.

    It has been revealed that boone and Edholm played to another low-scoring affair. But when you get 28 points from your kicker and D/ST, you're usually going to be in good shape. With Quinshon Judkins and Zach Charbonnet on bye, Edholm had to turn to Rachaad White, who laid an egg on MNF despite being active.

    According to recent reports, the hottest squad in the Expert League belongs to Joel Smyth, who has ripped off four wins in a row to get to 6-5 and has the second-most points in the league en route to a fifth-place standing. Unfortunately, Norris couldn't withstand Kenneth Walker III being out again and DK Metcalf being ejected against the Eagles.

    Sources indicate that eric Froton and Dan Titus topped the Week 11 scoreboard, each manager improving to 4-7. It just goes to show you that, even after a slow start, you can still salvage a season. Titus opened the season with five straight losses but has gone 4-2 over the past six.     #188062. Kushner-backed OakNorth secures U.S. bank charter as global digital banks push into America

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (637 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Kushner-backed OakNorth secures U.S. bank charter as global digital banks push into America

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (637 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The U.K.'s OakNorth has secured a federal bank charter, saying it is the first foreign digital bank to do so, as international competitors vie for U.S.
    • The charter clears OakNorth, which is backed by Jared Kushner's private equity firm, to acquire Michigan-based Community Unity Bank, subject to an $80 million capital injection, according to approval documents issued by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on Nov.
    • The deal, which is expected to close by the end of 2026, would allow OakNorth to provide loans, take deposits, and offer other banking services across all 50 states.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The U.K.'s OakNorth has secured a federal bank charter, saying it is the first foreign digital bank to do so, as international competitors vie for U.S. market share.

    The charter clears OakNorth, which is backed by Jared Kushner's private equity firm, to acquire Michigan-based Community Unity Bank, subject to an $80 million capital injection, according to approval documents issued by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on Nov. 19.

    The deal, which is expected to close by the end of 2026, would allow OakNorth to provide loans, take deposits, and offer other banking services across all 50 states.

    According to recent reports, kushner's private equity firm, Affinity Partners, took an 8% stake in OakNorth in 2025, with backing from major Gulf investors, including the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia and Qatar. SoftBank is also an OakNorth investor.

    The bank reported $295 million in pretax profit for 2025 in its annual report, up from $280 million the previous year and close to three times the $100 million in profits five years prior.

    It said principal losses on $20 billion in credit facilities issued over the past 10 years totaled £9 million, or less than 0.05%. Its 1.4% return on assets placed it among the top five banks in Western Europe and in the top 1% of commercial banks globally, according to The Banker's rankings.

    According to recent reports, "I would say that the level of animal spirits in the U.S. is always higher, right? So the momentum of business and the optimism is always a step up," OakNorth CEO Rishi Khosla told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Monday.

    In a recent development, he noted U.S. economic growth, investment in artificial intelligence and infrastructure spending would create opportunities for the bank.

    OakNorth has focused on lending to lower mid-market businesses rather than competing for consumer customers in a crowded U.S. market.

    It has been revealed that the lender targets businesses with annual revenues of $5 million to $100 million with loans worth $5 million to $50 million. The bank entered the U.S. market in 2023 and has lent about $3.5 billion to U.S. businesses to date. The U.S. accounted for 40% of its $12.4 billion in new loans in 2025.

    "These are really growth companies which are scaling up, and given that focus, you really haven't had an institution in the last decades that focus on that customer segment, and that's opened up the opportunity for us," Khosla noted.

    He cited commercial real estate lending as a particularly strong growth opportunity in the U.S.

    According to recent reports, securing the charter is notoriously difficult, with many regulatory hurdles. It took OakNorth 20 months, a restructure of the bank's corporate ownership, and relocating its holding organization from the island of Jersey to the U.K. to meet Federal Reserve requirements.

    In a recent development, other international fintechs seeking a foothold in the U.S. have struggled to gain traction. Monzo and Revolut withdrew their initial U.S. applications for a full banking charter between 2021 and 2023 after regulatory pushback.

    Monzo closed its U.S. operations in April just four years after it introduced, amid a crowded consumer market. "We have made a strategic decision to focus on scaling in our home market and Europe and to step away from the U.S.," the organization mentioned.

    But the regulatory landscape has since shifted. Revolut and Brazil's Nubank have received conditional approval for U.S. banking charters from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

    Dutch digital bank Bunq reapplied after withdrawing its 2023 application, but its second application was denied in August.

    Recent findings suggest that another U.K. digital lender, Starling, is also seeking U.S. growth. It sells its Engine banking software to mid-tier U.S. lenders and is looking to acquire a domestic bank to serve business clients.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton told reporters Tuesday that he is suspending veteran running back J.K.
    • Payton said it was due to "conduct detrimental to the team," and the head coach did not elaborate.
    • It has been revealed that dobbins is in his second season with the Broncos.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton told reporters Tuesday that he is suspending veteran running back J.K. Dobbins for Friday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

    Payton said it was due to "conduct detrimental to the team," and the head coach did not elaborate.

    It has been revealed that dobbins is in his second season with the Broncos. He began his career with the Baltimore Ravens and spent the 2024 season with the Los Angeles Chargers before joining Denver last year.

    He is right now the team's leading rusher with 324 yards and has three touchdowns on 99 carries.

    According to recent reports, the veteran running back played in 10 games last year, finishing with 772 yards and four touchdowns. Dobbins had a rookie in the backfield with him in RJ Harvey last year, and Denver brought in another this year in Jonah Coleman.

    Dobbins has noted he is happy to do whatever he can to contribute to the team, but last week Coleman had his breakout game with 111 yards and three touchdowns in Denver's 38-24 win over Las Vegas.

    Recent findings suggest that while Coleman had his best game as a rookie, Dobbins had only one touch. With Payton not elaborating, it is unclear whether the conduct detrimental to the team is related to his reduced role in the offense or coincidental.

    Coleman has promptly taken over as the lead back, with 302 yards and six touchdowns on 71 carries in six games.

    In a recent development, denver is the second-best team in the AFC, with an 8-2 record. The Broncos, who split with the Kansas City Chiefs this season, at the moment hold the tiebreaker over their AFC West rivals.

    In a recent development, the Broncos will take on the Steelers on the road on Black Friday. With no Dobbins, Coleman is expected to lead the backfield. Harvey and fellow running back Tyler Badie are right now on IR.

    Jaret Patterson and/or Cody Schrader will likely join Coleman in the backfield; both are currently on the practice squad and would need to be signed or elevated.

    #188052. Industry News: Op-ed: Trump’s Nvidia board intervention put a price on national security. Our adversaries will take note

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1675 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Op-ed: Trump’s Nvidia board intervention put a price on national security. Our adversaries will take note

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1675 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Trump has accomplished something extraordinary.
    • Sources indicate that on Monday, after Nvidia's board reinstated Huang following his resignation amid a counterintelligence controversy and allegations that Alice Huang, with whom he had an affair, is under suspicion of being a Chinese intelligence asset, Wall Street celebrated with a historic market bounce.
    • According to recent reports, what happened at Nvidia raises the frightening possibility that it does, and it fits a recent pattern that is exactly what geopolitical rivals around the world want to see.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald J. Trump has accomplished something extraordinary. He directly inserted himself into the boardroom of one of America's most strategically notable companies, Nvidia, helping to reverse a corporate leadership decision, and personally vouched for restored CEO Jensen Huang as having a clean bill of health regarding the national security investigations into his business activities with China.

    Sources indicate that on Monday, after Nvidia's board reinstated Huang following his resignation amid a counterintelligence controversy and allegations that Alice Huang, with whom he had an affair, is under suspicion of being a Chinese intelligence asset, Wall Street celebrated with a historic market bounce. But the market's enthusiasm should not obscure a far more consequential question circulating in Washington, D.C.: Does American national security have a price?

    According to recent reports, what happened at Nvidia raises the frightening possibility that it does, and it fits a recent pattern that is exactly what geopolitical rivals around the world want to see. Consider the economic pressures surrounding the Iran war. Disruptions to energy markets, shipping, supply chains, and consumer prices have complicated American strategic decision-making. These are notably different circumstances, but they raise the same troubling question about the costs of defending American national security interests, and when they become economically unpalatable to those in the Trump administration.

    Industry observers note that beijing, Tehran, and Moscow are watching — as are our allies and partners — and they all may agree on one thing: America has an Achilles' heel that military and technological superiority cannot overcome. It is possible to impose sufficient economic pain to alter Washington's strategic calculation with friends and foes alike. Bleed American capital markets, disrupt commerce, squeeze consumers, and eventually Washington may look for an exit.

    In a recent development, despite the narrative that the president is weaving, there is a fundamental difference between responsibly weighing economic consequences and allowing adversaries to conclude that they can impose an economic veto over U.S. national security policy. Trump told CNBC in an extensive interview on Monday morning that when it comes to national security, "losing the brain power of somebody like Jensen ... would be a far bigger threat than anything we're talking about.".

    According to recent reports, "The bigger impact was the long term. The bigger impact was you know he's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about, including me, that nobody else understands," Trump noted. "This was a significant loss. This was a tremendous loss. And you saw that it affected the market. It affected even, I think it even affected the perception of our country in the world," the president said.

    And that's true, but not only in the way Trump thinks it did.

    It has been revealed that this is not about whether Huang is a brilliant executive or whether Nvidia is enormously important to American competitiveness. Both are true. The question that America, particularly its government, must ask is whether Huang's economic importance justifies subordinating corporate governance, interfering with counterintelligence procedures, and stymying national security oversight.

    Sources indicate that trump characterized the Justice Department's assessment as having exonerated Huang. Yet Nvidia's board reinstated him while its own review remained open.

    Industry observers note that the allegations involving reported contacts with Chinese intelligence assets do not establish legal wrongdoing. However, presidential personal assurances are not substitutes for independent counterintelligence assessments and investigations or congressional oversight. Monday's rising stock price might only measure what shareholders believe Huang at the helm of Nvidia is worth, while discounting or ignoring the unresolved counterintelligence risk that he may still pose to Nvidia and the entire artificial intelligence ecosystem.

    The Trump administration, Silicon Valley, and Wall Street may believe the matter is closed.

    "That thing's like a rocket ship going in the wrong direction. Now it's a rocket ship going in the right direction, and it's taking the whole market," Trump told CNBC about Nvidia's 31.5% Monday gains.

    Industry observers note that one glaring vulnerability still on the horizon is what Washington does not know. If Beijing possesses additional damaging information, it controls whether, when, and how that information might be weaponized in an ongoing and now reignited strategic competition between the U.S. and China. Beijing retains the capacity to reopen this matter at a time of its choosing. Chinese intelligence could drip-feed disclosures, compel repeated explanations from Huang and the president, and transform Monday's declaration of resolution of this matter into a prolonged national security vulnerability.

    Sources indicate that there is also a striking irony here. Some pundits are comparing Trump's intervention to China's state-controlled market. To be sure, the Chinese government has a very heavy hand in its economy, but one thing the Chinese Communist Party will never do is put an individual ahead of national security and political authority despite the economic impact that this person or manufacturer is perceived to have. Xi Jinping and China's Communist Party have demonstrated a willingness to make almost the opposite calculation about national security and economic growth. Under Xi, national and political security generally takes precedence over the interests of individual companies and brilliant executives.

    According to recent reports, consider Jack Ma. In 2020, Beijing halted Ant Group's planned $37 billion initial public offering and subsequently imposed sweeping regulatory restrictions on Ma's business empire. Beijing accepted substantial economic consequences to reinforce national security and political authority. This is not an argument for importing China's authoritarian model into American corporate governance. But the strategic asymmetry is noteworthy to revisit in this latest comparative context. Beijing has demonstrated that even its most celebrated entrepreneurs are not indispensable to the party and the nation. Washington risks signaling that some of its entrepreneurs are in fact indispensable to the state, which ironically potentially makes them even bigger intelligence targets for foreign adversaries.

    It has been revealed that as an economic matter, the commercial realities of Nvidia's China business make this situation even more perplexing. China, including Hong Kong, accounted for just 9.1% of Nvidia's reported global revenue in fiscal 2026, down from 19.2% the previous year. Its latest fourth-quarter guidance assumes no Chinese data center compute revenue. Nvidia did change the way it reports geographic sales, to customer headquarter address, in late 2025. But anyone familiar with Chinese strategic documents, including the 15th Five-Year Proposal, should understand that Beijing has no intention of becoming permanently "addicted" to American chips. Its objective is technological self-reliance, not expanding Nvidia's market share and by extension its dependency on them.

    Sources indicate that whatever the exact figure, I cannot think of a number that is worth selling out U.S. national security over, but it certainly isn't  9.1%, which is also a number that will continue to shrink. Furthermore, if the AI ecosystem is critical to our economy and our national security, then selling advanced chips to China or loosening export controls is the opposite of what we should be doing because the chips are used to juice the compute of Chinese LLMs that compete with ours, and to increase the effectiveness and lethality of Chinese weapons systems. The questionable sales of Nvidia chips in Asia, which are at the heart of this story, support neither our economy nor our national security. They undermine them both.

    There is also an extraordinary corporate governance precedent that extends well beyond Nvidia and Huang, one that is escalating and growing more bold at each turn. While Trump has intervened in the markets before, in cases including U.S. Steel and Intel, he has never gone to this level, making the argument that a tech giant is so critical to the national security of the nation that at any point its decision making could require executive branch intervention and specific direction.

    Based on the president's rationale, what should the boards of key national security relevant companies like Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Palantir, Anduril, SpaceX, or even Rio Tinto — whose jointly owned Resolution Copper project in Arizona could eventually supply up to 25 percent of America's copper demand — expect? Does their strategic importance justify presidential intervention in executive appointments, succession planning, corporate strategy, or commercial relationships? A precedent established by one president becomes an idea, option, and instrument available to future presidents, including those with fundamentally different political preferences.

    All of this brings us to Congress. If you take Trump at his word, that Nvidia's strategic importance justifies extraordinary executive branch intervention, it also justifies extraordinary legislative intervention and oversight. Article I grants Congress authority to regulate foreign commerce. Congress established the statutory framework governing executive export-control authority through legislation, including the Export Control Reform Act of 2018. Those authorities were delegated, not surrendered. The president may have driven this Nvidia CEO decision by telephone. Congress possesses something more enduring: the authority to establish the rules through legislation. The Senate Banking Committee's scheduled December 3 hearing on export controls provides an opportunity to begin.

    Recent findings suggest that congress should do much more than demand classified briefings on the counterintelligence concerns. Lawmakers should pass, with veto-proof majorities, requirements for stronger board-level counterintelligence responsibilities, mandatory defensive briefings to vulnerable tech executives and innovation sector leadership, much tighter export-license oversight with enforcement mechanisms that have teeth, and enforceable reporting requirements. Legislative proposals including the AI Overwatch Act, Match Act, and Remote Access Security Act must be passed as soon as possible. Nvidia and its leadership may warrant considerably tighter legal and regulatory scrutiny given its importance as the fulcrum of the AI ecosystem.

    It is crucial for Congress to remember that the legislative branch is a co-equal branch of government, not a rubber stamp or talk shop providing us with commentary about the outcome of executive branch decisions. They have an active and constitutional role to play in our democracy. They need to get it together and get to work. If Nvidia is important enough for the president to enter its boardroom, it is important enough for Congress to exercise its constitutional authority over the rules governing this entire process.

    —By Dewardic McNeal, Managing Director and Senior Policy Analyst at Longview Global, and a CNBC Contributor.

    #188050. AG Blanche, FBI’s Patel dodge questions about Jensen Huang investigation

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (517 w)

    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    AG Blanche, FBI’s Patel dodge questions about Jensen Huang investigation

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (517 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel on Tuesday dodged questions about the conclusions of an investigation President Donald Trump cited to push Nvidia's board to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO.
    • Asked by a reporter whether the Department of Justice had investigated Huang and the results of that probe, Blanche noted, "What the president said is that he talked to a lot of people going into the decision that he made to encourage the board to reinstate him.".
    • "And so I'm not going to get into communications I have with the president," Blanche noted at a news conference in Washington.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel on Tuesday dodged questions about the conclusions of an investigation President Donald Trump cited to push Nvidia's board to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO.

    Asked by a reporter whether the Department of Justice had investigated Huang and the results of that probe, Blanche noted, "What the president said is that he talked to a lot of people going into the decision that he made to encourage the board to reinstate him.".

    "And so I'm not going to get into communications I have with the president," Blanche noted at a news conference in Washington.

    Industry observers note that huang was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia on Monday morning, less than two weeks after resigning amid allegations he had affairs with a purported spy for China and two Nvidia employees plus concerns that advanced semiconductor chips made by his manufacturer had been diverted to China in violation of U.S. law.

    In an interview with CNBC on Monday, Trump was asked what led him to personally confirm to Nvidia's board that Huang was not a national security risk.

    "We've done a very thorough investigation, and the investigation showed that he did, I mean, he had bad judgment having to do with somewhat unrelated incidents, but he did nothing wrong," Trump replied.

    According to recent reports, trump in a Truth Social post on Monday mentioned the U.S. government had no reason to believe Huang's return to the company "poses any risk to National Security," and that Blanche had confirmed the government "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    In a recent development, nvidia, in its statement Monday announcing Huang's return, noted, "The Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk.".

    Blanche on Tuesday said, "Nvidia is a good corporate citizen.".

    "Obviously, if Nvidia was the target, or was the subject of some criminal investigation, or they were obstructing or thwarting our investigation, then that wouldn't be the message that the president is saying to the American people," he stated.

    Industry observers note that patel did not answer a reporter's question of whether the FBI has spoken to Huang and whether the FBI had been made aware of an assessment by U.S. intelligence agencies that Huang's reported paramour, Alice Huang, was an asset for China's spy agency.

    Jensen Huang is not related to Alice Huang, who was an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of Nvidia's semiconductor chips.

    The DOJ and Commerce Department on Nov. 17 remarked they were investigating Megaspeed for potential diversion of Nvidia chips in violation of U.S. export law.

    Asked how the DOJ could rule out Jensen Huang having potential criminal liability given the fact that the investigation remains ongoing, Blanche replied, "So, when you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don't know what you're talking about.".

    "We have hundreds, if not more, export investigations going at any time at the Department of Justice," Blanche said.

    Tech Report: Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest was a significant buyer of Anthropic as she tells CNBC she’s ‘quite optimistic’

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (412 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.
    • Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence firm in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.
    • Industry observers note that "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence firm in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    Industry observers note that "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    In a recent development, anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    "We're climbing a wall of worry," stated Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, new technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    The Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood remarked she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    In her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    Ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the big losses.

    Sources indicate that the fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    In a recent development, "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she said. "That's how crazy things were.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A quick fantasy basketball breakdown on all 30 teams after Week 5 of the 2026-27 NBA season.

    In a recent development, spurs: Victor Wembanyama dominated Saturday: 50 points, 19 rebounds, 5 blocks and 4 steals in 32 minutes of a 114-91 win over the Pelicans. It got him the High Score of the week, with 97 fantasy points. He's the first player since 1973-74 with a 50/15/5/4 game (since steals and blocks became official stats). It's his second 50 piece this month (52 on Nov. 4), and San Antonio is 15-3 on the season with Wemby leading the way as the top player in fantasy.

    According to recent reports, bulls: Josh Giddey posted 23 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high 22 assists in Sunday's 151-145 OT loss to Denver, the league's first 20-20 game this season. Giddey followed up that epic game with a 2-for-11 performance with 4 points, 11 assists, 2 stocks and 3 turnovers on Monday. He was benched in crunch time (again). If you have Giddey, I'd sell. The game-to-game variance is too erratic.

    According to recent reports, heat: Bam Adebayo posted 24 points, 15 rebounds and a career-high 12 assists with zero turnovers in Sunday's 123-113 win over OKC with Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin) out. Miami has won seven straight to reach 10-6. Shout-out to Klay Thompson, who averaged 20.7 points and 5.1 3s over a recent seven-game stretch and is closing in on Ray Allen for third all time in 3s. Keep holding Klay in 12s.

    Bucks: Tyler Herro set a new career high in Philly on Saturday, dropping 50 points, then added 32 with 8 assists in Monday's win in Toronto to snap a 13-game skid. At 2-16, start prepping for some shakeups in the rotation — which could impact vets like Herro, Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner. Rookie Brayden Burries (40% rostered) had 14 points, 10 boards, and 4 assists off the bench Monday, and should be rostered in most leagues.

    In a recent development, cavaliers: James Harden dropped 51 in Friday's 128-119 win over Indiana, passing Kobe Bryant for the third-most 50-point games ever (26). Evan Mobley (toe) has missed six straight and is due for re-evaluation this week. Kenny Atkinson has started Tyrese Proctor and Sam Merrill over the past week, but rookie Meleek Thomas (13.3 points in 24 minutes) is still the best streamer here.

    Nets: Nolan Traore (right hamstring) will be re-evaluated in 8-10 weeks. Mikel Brown Jr. (19% rostered) got the first crack, starting Monday in Minnesota with his minutes restriction lifted: 17 points, a career-high 7 assists and 5 boards in 29 minutes. Egor Demin shot 3-for-13 off the bench. Brown is the add over Demin. The No. 6 pick has a path to 30 minutes a night.

    Industry observers note that lakers: Austin Reaves (left heel) practiced fully on Sunday and is targeting a return on Friday in San Antonio. Quentin Grimes averaged 9.2 points through 12 games, then moved into the starting lineup over the last five games, averaging 24.8 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 3.4 assists. He ranks 31st in 9-cat over that span, with 35.58 fantasy points per game.

    Sources indicate that enjoy it now, because he won't see anywhere near 37 minutes a night when Reaves returns. Matisse Thybulle is the keeper. His 39 steals rank second in the league, and he and Wemby are the only players this year with 15+ blocks, 20+ steals and 30+ 3s.

    Hawks: Atlanta has won four straight without CJ McCollum, whose left calf strain will be re-evaluated in about four weeks. No. 8 pick Kingston Flemings got next, but don't rush to get him because the Hawks won't play until Friday.

    In a recent development, dyson Daniels, though? He's such a unique fantasy talent. He's posting 9.5 points, 7.4 boards, 5.6 assists and a league-leading 2.9 steals per night. He can't shoot beyond 10 feet, but he's touching nearly every major counting-stats category except blocks and 3s.

    Recent findings suggest that grizzlies: No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer (ankle) will be re-evaluated in four weeks. That hurts. Kris Murray started in his absence on Monday, playing 32 minutes and got 5 stocks. Add him to the watchlist, even though Memphis will likely form a committee between Murray, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant (when he gets back). Make sure Cam Spencer (45%) isn't on waivers.

    Sources indicate that clippers: Brandon Ingram started in his debut Monday in Houston and posted 16 points, 7 boards, and 4 assists in 27 minutes. The shooting was unsurprisingly rough (6-for-18, 0-for-6 from three), but 18 shots in his first game since May is a great sign. Marc Stein reported that LA is showcasing vets like Rui Hachimura and Kris Dunn before the trade deadline.

    According to recent reports, jazz: Svi Mykhailiuk went OFF Sunday for 39 points and 10 threes, both career highs. I'd rather pick up Ace Bailey, though.

    Sources indicate that 76ers: Philly's five-game win streak ended Monday against Portland with Joel Embiid (illness) out. Embiid's been better, and fantasy managers could take the opportunity to float offers because health is always the biggest question mark with Embiid.

    In a recent development, celtics: Four straight losses. Derrick White is shooting 40.1% from the field and 28.8% from 3, well off his 45.4/38.7 peak. I'm holding in 9-cat, but it's been a disappointing start.

    Sources indicate that mavericks: Just two games this week, and two scheduled before the NBA Cup next week. Cut fringe Mavs for players who play more games over the next two weeks.

    Knicks: Josh Hart is averaging 6.6 points on 34/27/60 shooting. Woof.

    Sources indicate that pistons: Over the past five games, Ausar Thompson ranks 16th in 9-cat. He's making 87.5% of his free throws (albeit low volume, but still!).

    According to recent reports, magic: Anthony Black continues to lap Jalen Suggs. Suggs is averaging 9-5-4 with 35/29/73 shooting splits. He's down to 73% rostered, but fantasy managers should stay patient as he ramps up from a bone bruise injury that cost him eight games.

    Sources indicate that wizards: The Wizards want Trae Young to focus less on scoring and more on passing. Per Kevin O'Connor, Young had 8 minutes of possession time per game over his first 6 games. It's down to 5 minutes over his last 5 games.

    Industry observers note that raptors: Toronto lost to the 2-16 Bucks and sits at 6-11 overall. Kawhi Leonard (knee) is shooting at practice but is still a couple of weeks away from returning. Jakob Poeltl is back on the radar after averaging 11.0 points, 9.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.3 steals, and 1.3 blocks in 29.7 minutes per game in his last three games.

    Pacers: At 5-12 without Tyrese Haliburton, Indiana is reportedly looking to make a move. In the meantime, Kelly Oubre Jr. (36%) should be rostered in all leagues.

    Sources indicate that hornets: Brandon Miller and Coby White sat all of OT in a four-point loss to the Lakers last week. Minutes restrictions are costing teams Ws.

    Timberwolves: Rudy Gobert ranks 114th in points leagues and 290th in 9-cat. His efficiency near the rim is pacing to his worst since his rookie season — he's 17-for-53 on layups through Monday. Plus, his rebounding and block rates are tumbling. Keep an eye on Joan Beringer.

    Rockets: At 13-5, Houston owns the NBA's best offensive rating (121.1) and a plus-8.2 net rating (5th in the league).

    Sources indicate that nuggets: Nikola Jokić logged triple-double No. 202 on Sunday. He's seven behind Russell Westbrook's record.

    Trail Blazers: Donovan Clingan is finishing 74% at the rim, up from 66% last season.

    It has been revealed that thunder: Nearly 80% of Ajay Mitchell's shots are 2s and he's hitting 28.3% from 3. He'll need to extend that range if the Thunder want to right the ship.

    Suns: Four straight wins after Monday's OT victory in Latest Orleans. If Jalen Green was dropped in a points league, pick him up.

    Warriors: Stephen Curry (oblique) is due for re-evaluation this week.

    Pelicans: New Orleans sits at 5-14, so it's a team to watch by the deadline. Keep holding the young guys, Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen. Everyone else could be on the block.

    It has been revealed that kings: Keegan Murray has 12-plus points and seven-plus boards in four of his last five. Rounding into form? Maybe.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It's Thanksgiving week in the NFL and there's a lot to go over, both on the injury front and the schedule.
    • It has been revealed that so Week 12 is spread across five different days, which can be pretty hectic for fantasy football managers.
    • Herbert: The Chargers have shown signs of life over the past two weeks, scoring 23 and 24 points, respectively.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It's Thanksgiving week in the NFL and there's a lot to go over, both on the injury front and the schedule. The Packers and Rams play Wednesday night, while we have the usual three-game Thanksgiving lineup. We also have the Broncos and Steelers on Black Friday, then the normal Sunday slate and Monday Night Football.

    It has been revealed that so Week 12 is spread across five different days, which can be pretty hectic for fantasy football managers. We're here to help out, taking you through the NFL injury report with the latest updates and some fantasy analysis for key players.

    Justin Herbert, LAC (concussion protocol).

    Drake Maye, NE (leg) — Out at least six weeks.

    Herbert: The Chargers have shown signs of life over the past two weeks, scoring 23 and 24 points, respectively. Herbert turned in his first QB1 finish of the 2026 season with 22.44 fantasy points against the Jets on Sunday. He only had 131 passing yards, two TDs, 32 rushing yards and another score on the ground, so it isn't like "we are so back" or anything. But now Herbert will need to clear concussion protocol in order to play Week 12 against the Patriots, another solid matchup.

    Recent findings suggest that with how the QB landscape is right now, if Herbert can clear, he isn't a bad add as a QB2 or streaming option for Week 12. The Chargers have some winnable matchups down the stretch and Herbert will likely need to throw. Maybe Herbert and the Chargers can still salvage something for fantasy.

    Sources indicate that darnold: The reigning Super Bowl champ has missed the past two games but has a shot to get back on the field for Week 12 against the 49ers in a major spot. Seattle is coming off its bye and Drew Lock has been the starter. He's been more than serviceable, undefeated in essentially four starts this season. There's not much difference between Darnold and Lock starting for fantasy managers. Whoever starts will be a QB2 this week, and either way, Jaxon Smith-Njigba will get fed.

    Bhayshul Tuten, JAX (lower body).

    Josh Jacobs, GB (finger) — Unlikely to play in Week 12.

    In a recent development, J.K. Dobbins, DEN (suspension) — Won't play in Week 12.

    Walker: The Chiefs' lead back missed his second straight game Sunday, though the team didn't miss him much. Kansas City rolled to another easy win over the Cardinals, 34-7. Emmett Johnson led the backfield again with another strong performance, racking up 143 total yards, four catches and a score for 22.3 fantasy points. Johnson has RB1 finishes in three of his past four games.

    In a recent development, the Chiefs take on the Bills in a highly anticipated matchup on Thanksgiving night. Walker will have a short week to get ready to return, which isn't ideal. He was limited at practice on Tuesday. If Walker sits again, Johnson can be fired up as an RB1 in what should be a high-scoring affair. If Walker is able to play, we could see him eased back into action given how well Johnson has fared in his stead. In that scenario, Walker would return to RB1/2 status while Johnson would hold value as a flex play.

    Tuten: The Jaguars took a tough loss in Week 11 to the Giants and lost Tuten late in the game with an undisclosed injury. He had been dealing with an ankle issue coming into the contest, so it could have something to do with that. Either way, Tuten has been playing pretty banged up over the last handful of games.

    If Tuten ends up missing Week 12, Chris Rodriguez Jr. would likely take over the backfield. He had four carries for 28 yards against Latest York, and has four rushing TDs on the season. C-Rod would basically be elevated to RB2 status with a matchup against the Titans in Week 12. If Tuten is active, you have to play him but know there's some risk given the injuries.

    Davante Adams, LAR (hamstring) — Out until at least Week 13.

    Marvin Harrison Jr., HOU (hamstring).

    A.J. Brown, NE (hamstring) — Likely out.

    Bowers: The Raiders were without their top offensive weapon for a loss to the Broncos on Sunday afternoon in Week 11. It felt like a long shot for Bowers to be ready but there's optimism he'll be back for Week 12 against the Browns. Fernando Mendoza looked better in his second NFL start, which is encouraging for Bowers' fantasy prospects. If Bowers is active, you're playing him. If he's out, there aren't any teams on bye, so there should be plenty of streaming options, including Michael Mayer, though he was quiet with just one catch for four yards on Sunday.

    Kincaid: It's been another up-and-down, injury-impacted campaign for the Bills' tight end. He missed his first game of the season in Week 11 against the Dolphins but had been popping up on the injury report most weeks. He told reporters Tuesday he'll "most likely" play Thursday night against K.C. Since his hot start, Kincaid only had one game with double-digit fantasy points in the past seven games. Dawson Knox got a few catches against Miami but isn't really a viable streaming option if Kincaid is out again for Thursday night's game against the Chiefs.

    Puka Nacua, WR, LAR (knee) — Out for season.

    Utah drops criminal charges against Kalshi founders after company suspended operations in state

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Utah on Tuesday dismissed criminal charges against Kalshi and its two co-founders following the decision by the prediction market platform on Monday to suspend operations in the state.
    • The state originally filed the 14 criminal charges against the organization and founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara on Oct.
    • The Commodity Futures Trading Commission — the federal regulator for prediction markets which views itself as the sole body that can develop rules over the growing industry — sued Utah the day before the state confirmed its charges.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Utah on Tuesday dismissed criminal charges against Kalshi and its two co-founders following the decision by the prediction market platform on Monday to suspend operations in the state.

    The state originally filed the 14 criminal charges against the organization and founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara on Oct. 28, claiming that Kalshi operated an illegal gambling operation in the state.

    The Commodity Futures Trading Commission — the federal regulator for prediction markets which views itself as the sole body that can develop rules over the growing industry — sued Utah the day before the state confirmed its charges.

    It has been revealed that mansour and Lara were slated to appear in a Utah district court on Dec. 4, according to court documents.

    However, Kalshi suspended operations in Utah on Monday, citing legal uncertainty. Utah Attorney General Derek Brown celebrated the decision in a statement announcing the move to dismiss the state's charges.

    Industry observers note that "Every tech giant in this space should take note," he mentioned. "If they promote, support, or enable gambling, we will hold them accountable.".

    Brown's office noted in the statement that dismissal is without prejudice, meaning if Kalshi were to begin operations again in the state the charges could be refiled.

    "Good faith jurisdictional disagreements should never be criminalized," Kalshi's general counsel Yaakov Roth said in a post on X. "We stand ready to work with State AGs on reasonable interim measures until courts resolve the dispute over who regulates prediction markets.".

    While Kalshi faces legal setbacks in Utah, it faced some relief in New York on Monday when a state judge denied an emergency temporary restraining order against the company to halt its operations in the jurisdiction. The court will hear arguments on the matter again in January.

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.
