    #188036. Congress shreds Nvidia's 'outrageous' decision to bring back Huang: 'Failure of character'

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1214 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Congress shreds Nvidia's 'outrageous' decision to bring back Huang: 'Failure of character'

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1214 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Members of Congress from both parties on Monday expressed outrage and incredulity, and doubled down on their calls for investigations, after Nvidia unveiled it has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO.
    • The resurrection of Huang, who had resigned from the artificial intelligence behemoth just 11 days earlier, raises more questions about the organization's decision-making and the Trump administration's national security assessments, on top of existing concerns about Nvidia's advanced AI chips being diverted to China, the lawmakers remarked.
    • "It's inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO," Rep.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Members of Congress from both parties on Monday expressed outrage and incredulity, and doubled down on their calls for investigations, after Nvidia unveiled it has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO.

    The resurrection of Huang, who had resigned from the artificial intelligence behemoth just 11 days earlier, raises more questions about the organization's decision-making and the Trump administration's national security assessments, on top of existing concerns about Nvidia's advanced AI chips being diverted to China, the lawmakers remarked.

    "It's inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO," Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., a China hawk who is retiring from Congress, told CNBC in a phone interview. "To me it's a failure of character.".

    President Donald Trump told CNBC in an extended interview later Monday morning that he personally intervened to convince Nvidia's board to bring Huang back, saying, "I made the deal.".

    Bacon, chairman of the House Subcommittee on Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation, said he wants the next Congress to conduct thorough oversight, while questioning the Trump administration's motives.

    Recent findings suggest that "Somebody's responsible for this, and it may be" Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whose department is responsible for setting U.S. export controls on AI chips, Bacon mentioned. "But I think we should get to the bottom of this.".

    In a recent development, huang, who is scheduled to testify before multiple committees on Capitol Hill starting Dec. 1, is "going to get high scrutiny in a bipartisan way when he comes next week," Bacon noted.

    Huang's closed-door appearance before a trio of House committees is on the schedule, as the panels seek answers on the national security implications of Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, MS NOW reported. The Senate banking committee unveiled after Huang's reinstatement that he will appear for a public hearing Dec. 3.

    John Fisher of Trident, a spokesman for Huang, declined to comment on the Nvidia CEO's scheduled appearances.

    Sources indicate that "He better be there," Rep. Gabe Amo, D-R.I., a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told CNBC about Huang's scheduled Dec. 1 appearance. His reinstatement will only intensify congressional probes into Nvidia and its government connections, Amo predicted.

    "I think it frankly broadens the scope of the query, and it makes Howard Lutnick and his dealings — supporting his nepo children's operation at Cantor Fitzgerald — party to inquiry as well as any other administration official that has facilitated a status quo in which chips can be sold to China or Chinese operated intermediaries who don't intend good things for the American people," remarked Amo, referring to the financial firm run by Lutnick's sons that has business ties to Nvidia.

    A Cantor spokesperson didn't comment directly when asked about Amo's comments, saying the firm "holds no material proprietary position in Nvidia" and noting its Nvidia positions "arise primarily from equity swaps executed for clients.".

    The Commerce Department didn't immediately respond to requests to comment on Bacon's and Amo's remarks.

    Nvidia in a statement Monday stated it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

    David Rudenstine, a constitutional law professor and national security scholar at Cardozo School of Law, said the frenzy around Huang's comeback is secondary to lingering national security concerns."The real responsibility for national security is with the administration and not with the CEO of a private company," Rudenstine told CNBC."You're opposed to China getting the chips. You recognize that the intermediary companies are sending chips to China, and you don't put a stop to it. I don't get it," he said.

    The CEO's reinstatement, while celebrated by the White House and in Silicon Valley, led to heightened calls on Capitol Hill to seek answers on AI chip exports to China and what the Trump administration's role has been in facilitating that.

    It has been revealed that "We are sending high-end computer chips to China, and yet we're saying we want to win the AI war. It's a contradiction, and it's a failure of leadership in the White House," Bacon told CNBC.

    Sen. Ron Wyden of Oregon, the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, told CNBC in an emailed statement that Huang's return "proves that under Trump, Vance, and Rubio, national security is for sale to the highest bidder.".

    Sources indicate that "We will all pay the price of letting China plunder America's cutting edge technology. Democrats will be pushing for accountability for anyone in the administration that put corrupt deals over our country's security," Wyden, who is also a Senate Intelligence Committee member, said.

    Sources indicate that trump in a Truth Social post Monday added that Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    Lawmakers, who have already launched multiple investigations related to Huang, Nvidia and related entities, quickly filed in to question those conclusions.

    In a recent development, sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., a close Trump ally and a former CEO, criticized the move and called for a congressional briefing "as soon as possible" on Huang's reinstatement.

    It has been revealed that "Nvidia's board is free to vote however they want, but the federal government owes the American people answers about what actually happened," Scott told CNBC in an emailed statement. "This looks terrible on its face, and it drives home the need for Congress to be informed on the full impact of Jensen Huang's actions on our national security and economy.".

    It has been revealed that rep. Scott Peters, D-Calif., a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, told CNBC that it's still not clear to what degree Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy might have compromised national security.

    "The fact that the president of the United States is involved in putting him back in there, presumably because maybe he has stock or he just cares about the stock market, it's really reached a bizarre place," Peters remarked. "And obviously that man has not learned anything from the election about what people think of him, or he doesn't care.".

    Monday's move also gave fuel to lawmakers who have already questioned Trump, his administration or Nvidia.

    "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the organization's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., said in a statement via the Senate Banking Committee, where she is the top Democrat and is expected to become chair in January.

    Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, more tersely questioned the official assurances that Huang poses no risks to national security.

    "No national security risk? Based on what?" he wrote on X.

    Recent findings suggest that rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, D-Ill., who serves on the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, in an X post called Nvidia's decision to reinstate Huang "outrageous.".

    "We still don't know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia's own board has completed its investigation," wrote Krishnamoorthi, who is also a member of the House Oversight and Intelligence panels.

    — CNBC's Dan Mangan, Garrett Downs and Luke Fountain contributed to this report.

    #188032. Peterson: Here’s what Bessent’s about-face on Jensen Huang reveals about Trump and China

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (897 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Peterson: Here’s what Bessent’s about-face on Jensen Huang reveals about Trump and China

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (897 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • For a minute there, it seemed like someone in the Trump administration might actually be willing to stand up to China.
    • Sources indicate that for about a week and a half, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was the face of an emerging harder line on Nvidia over the potential risks its co-founder Jensen Huang's affairs posed to national security.
    • According to recent reports, they see China's AI program as a major threat, and want to restrain its growth by cutting off the supply of advanced chips to China.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    For a minute there, it seemed like someone in the Trump administration might actually be willing to stand up to China.

    Sources indicate that for about a week and a half, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was the face of an emerging harder line on Nvidia over the potential risks its co-founder Jensen Huang's affairs posed to national security. Bessent was giving voice to China hawks who had felt sidelined by the Trump administration's willingness to sell artificial intelligence chips to  China.

    According to recent reports, they see China's AI program as a major threat, and want to restrain its growth by cutting off the supply of advanced chips to China. The resignation of Huang, who pressed the Trump Administration to allow the exports, seemed to signal that the hawks had found latest influence in Washington.

    According to recent reports, by this weekend, Bessent had softened his public resistance to Huang's reinstatement. That came just in time for Nvidia's board to reappoint Huang as CEO at President Donald Trump's urging.

    Whether any real damage was done to national security isn't clear. But it is safe to say that the incoming Democratic majority in Congress won't take Trump at his word when he said on CNBC Monday that the Department of Justice "did a pretty good investigation" that exonerated Huang.

    Congress will look deeply into the worries Bessent himself raised about Huang's acknowledged romantic relationship with a woman The New York Times and others have reported was a Chinese intelligence asset.

    It has been revealed that nvidia's board remarked it had received assurances from top U.S. officials and had concluded his return wasn't a national security risk.

    A top concern is whether China was able to use the affair to help divert Nvidia's high-end artificial intelligence chips toward helping its military. Bessent in a Nov. 13 interview with CNBC outlined the stakes.

    "Any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts the — it hurts our great companies and in the AI race it gives the Chinese an advantage," he said.

    Recent findings suggest that bessent noted that his department and others had wanted to blacklist Megaspeed, the firm previously run by Alice Huang, Jensen Huang's paramour. But "Commerce has the pen," Bessent said.

    The Commerce Department is headed by Secretary Howard Lutnick, Bessent's rival.

    Putting Huang back at Nvidia wasn't originally Bessent's preference. He mentioned in a Fox interview on Nov. 15 that the board should "go outside the organization" to find a new leader. But by this past weekend, Bessent had apparently gotten on board with Trump's wishes.

    "Jensen is on the outside now," Bessent told CBS on Sunday, in trying to explain his apparent policy shift.

    Commerce has since taken steps to tighten some restrictions meant to prevent U.S. chips from helping China advance in the AI race.

    It has been revealed that but there is bipartisan worry about the Nvidia episode. "I think we need to catalog the damage that's been done," Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., told The Wall Street Journal. He said Lutnick had not responded to letters he sent saying the administration should be "taking the threats of communist China more seriously.".

    According to recent reports, but Trump has clearly put an upper limit on how aggressively anyone in his administration can push back on China. The president remarked Monday that he was swayed by the pageantry in his visit to China last week.

    Xi "met me at the plane, which is something they've never done, which was a sign," Trump said.

    Trump mentioned he felt like he needed to intervene to back Huang because the stock market was plummeting in the wake of Nvidia's troubles — a development he also blamed on Democrats' midterm victory.

    "I watched our country lose $5 trillion because of a bad election," he noted. "If I didn't get involved, you'd probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come." Now, its stock performance will be "unbelievable.".

    Bessent on Sunday played down the market risks. The tech giant "continues to be fantastically profitable, and there is near unlimited demand for their chips worldwide," he told CBS.

    Recent findings suggest that lutnick has embraced Trump's transactional urges. He has backed deals in which the U.S. takes equity stakes in companies such as Intel, saying the taxpayer deserves some of the upside.

    Lutnick in January remarked he had heard Huang pitch Trump on allowing Nvidia to sell its relatively more advanced H200 chips into China.

    Sources indicate that "There are strong — two sides. We shouldn't sell them any or we should sell them." Where does he stand? "Right in the middle," Lutnick told Bloomberg. Trump decided to go ahead with the deal.

    Bessent has stated he is "neither a hawk nor a dove" on China, and is simply trying to manage the ultra-sensitive relationship between the world's two biggest economies. But the upshot of the Huang affair seems to be that Bessent wasn't able to sway the president on a matter that seemed cut-and-dried just days ago.

    Lutnick, meanwhile, is riding high.

    According to recent reports, trump remarked he discussed whether Huang should return to Nvidia with Lutnick, Bessent and Vice President JD Vance. "Howard Lutnick was very good. Very, he's very professional," Trump said on CNBC Monday.

    "I call them the opposites, Scott and Howard," Trump added, before declaring them "both good.".

    #188029. As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (436 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (436 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • It has been revealed that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Sources indicate that as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    It has been revealed that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the upcoming tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders major and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," said Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".

    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic shares fall below IPO price. Traders see even more pain

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (380 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that anthropic shares are back trading below the IPO price after a 13% sell-off Tuesday and a 1.5% drop Monday, despite a broad rally in most massive tech artificial intelligence names.
    • It took just four days for ANT to fall under its offering price, compared with 21 trading days for SpaceX, which rallied out of the gate.
    • According to recent reports, options volume on the stock is picking up as the shares drop and implied volatility jumps to 96, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic shares are back trading below the IPO price after a 13% sell-off Tuesday and a 1.5% drop Monday, despite a broad rally in most massive tech artificial intelligence names. Trading under $76 on Tuesday, the stock's now 8.5% below its initial public offering level and 34% beneath its intraday high of $115.

    It took just four days for ANT to fall under its offering price, compared with 21 trading days for SpaceX, which rallied out of the gate.

    According to recent reports, options volume on the stock is picking up as the shares drop and implied volatility jumps to 96, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Almost 500,000 options traded by noon ET on Tuesday for a total premium of about $250 million, the sixth-most active single-stock options in the market, SpotGamma data indicates.

    Almost 300,000 puts traded versus about 200,000 calls, but the sentiment implied by the trades was not overtly bearish, and judging by the biggest single trades of the day, traders are divided on what happens next.

    In a recent development, the biggest single option trade of the day was a $7.5 million purchase of almost 11,000 75-strike puts expiring in mid-December. The trader paid above the ask, suggesting an eagerness to get the trade done at a cost of $6.85, according to SpotGamma. With Anthropic trading at $77, the position needs Anthropic to drop 11% by expiry to pay off.

    "Anthropic remains bumpy as investors add risk to other names," said noted tech analyst Dan Ives.

    Only one obvious call purchase appeared among the top 10 trades: a 3,000-lot purchase of 85-strike calls expiring Jan. 15 that cost $7.10 each, for a total of $2.2 million. That trade needs Anthropic to rally 19% within the next two months to break even.

    According to recent reports, arguably the most interesting action was a string of almost a dozen put sales, ranging from $400,000 to $1.6 million each, all within moments of each other, selling the 120-strike puts expiring Dec. 18. The puts bring in $40 each, meaning the breakeven for the trade is at $80. Selling in-the-money puts in high-volatility stocks is often a way for traders to get long stock without the capital requirements of buying the underlying equity.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.
    • On platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026.
    • Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    On platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    Recent findings suggest that on Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    "The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note said.

    It has been revealed that the Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

    It has been revealed that in that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    How Meta is using Instagram to get an ad boost from its Muse personal AI agent

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (462 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Meta's ad-free Muse personal artificial intelligence agent is already helping the social media giant boost its advertising business, and it's happening through Instagram, multiple people told CNBC.
    • Instagram is a major advertising revenue engine for the social media giant, and the organization is leveraging existing habits on the platform by prompting people to organize their saved posts in Muse.
    • About 20% of daily Instagram owners save at least one post to the app per day, according to a person familiar with the details, who asked not to be named because the information is not public.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Meta's ad-free Muse personal artificial intelligence agent is already helping the social media giant boost its advertising business, and it's happening through Instagram, multiple people told CNBC.

    Instagram is a major advertising revenue engine for the social media giant, and the organization is leveraging existing habits on the platform by prompting people to organize their saved posts in Muse.

    About 20% of daily Instagram owners save at least one post to the app per day, according to a person familiar with the details, who asked not to be named because the information is not public. Many of those saved items, the person said, are either shoppable items or ads.

    A senior executive told CNBC that Muse, even without ads, "is still very valuable for our ads business because it raises conversions for advertisers." It does this by reducing friction in the shopping process and allowing owners to go back to items later, said the executive, who asked not to be named because the details have not been reported publicly.

    "It gives advertisers a way to get more ROI for the dollars they're already spending, and that's all because Muse is helping people shop," the executive said.

    Mark Zuckerberg unveiled in Meta's last earnings call that 25% of Muse's customers shop via the agentic tool — it's the most common use case for Muse — and the average purchase price is over $200. Zuckerberg stated the manufacturer aims to take a small fee from transactions made through the agentic platform.

    All that information about what people are shopping for with their agent is a valuable asset to target ads more precisely within Instagram. If consumers complete purchases with their Muse, that builds Meta's latest revenue stream.

    Meta's efforts to drive transactions seem to be paying off, and the buzz around Muse has made it a leader in agentic shopping.

    It has been revealed that in the week ending Nov. 22, 51% of all agentic orders were done by Meta's Muse, according to transactions measured by Forter Intelligence, an e-commerce analytics and cybertechnology manufacturer.

    Recent findings suggest that meta dominates agentic AI shopping market share, according to Forter, which mentioned that SpaceX's Grok held a 24% market share in that same time period, followed by 22% to OpenAI's ChatGPT. The remaining 3% is divided between Google and startup Instinct.

    Meta is expected to eventually launch ads in Muse, though multiple people mentioned that it's not under any financial pressure to do so and tends to take its time building an audience before monetizing it.

    The people mentioned that putting ads in the Muse feed, which is more akin to a newsfeed instead of responses to specific queries, would be a natural way for Meta to test ads on the platform.

    The Nasdaq is in freefall. Here's one stock to look at

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, I asked Claude after Friday's close what I should do about the tanking stock market.
    • Amazon's cloud business is growing at its fastest pace in nearly five years.
    • AWS demand supports the lower end of the range.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, I asked Claude after Friday's close what I should do about the tanking stock market. Its advice was surprisingly useful: avoid panic selling and look for opportunities. A 40 VIX, which it touched Friday, might provide those opportunities. Specifically, a higher VIX (higher options premiums) signals fear, but it also creates an opportunity to sell elevated premium in some premium stocks, like Amazon.

    Amazon's cloud business is growing at its fastest pace in nearly five years. AWS revenue rose 39.3% YoY in the third quarter, and management reported a $578 billion backlog. Trailing 12-month operating cash flow rose 29% to $168.3 billion. However, infrastructure investment accelerated, resulting in more than $42 billion in negative cash flow. The competing forces of accelerating growth and the cost of supplying it could keep the stock in its range over the next four weeks. Its shares are only off 14% from its recent highs, comparatively better than the Nasdaq Composite's near 19% decline.

    AWS demand supports the lower end of the range. The backlog gives Amazon a basis for adding capacity even as investors scrutinize the cash cost. Cash spending could temper an upside rerating.

    The next leg higher may require evidence that newly introduced capacity can earn attractive returns at this scale, and that evidence may be in short supply over the next couple of months.

    In a recent development, sell the Dec. 18, 2026 AMZN 235/285 strangle for an indicative $5.90 credit per share.

    Max reward — $590 per strangle if AMZN finishes between $235 and $285 at expiration, before fees.

    Breakevens at expiration — $229.10 and $290.90.

    Recent findings suggest that max risk — Unlimited on the uncovered call, but one should think of the trade as risking getting short at a net price above $290, a nearly 13% premium to today's closing price. The downside loss would reach $22,910 per strangle if AMZN fell to zero. The credit is roughly 2.3% of a $260 reference share price over four weeks, or nearly 30% on a simple annualized basis. That comparison uses the share price as its denominator. Actual return on capital depends on margin and the cost to close or settle the trade.

    Recent findings suggest that buying in bear markets, as the Nasdaq just touched, is never easy. But those opportunities don't present themselves too often. What are you going to do with it?

    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    CNBC's The China Connection newsletter: AI race spreads from robots to smartphones

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (915 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing.
    • Sources indicate that I'm just back from APEC in Shenzhen, where I saw the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia gather along with other member economies.
    • It only took a few months for a humanoid robot to get better at picking up household items.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing. Welcome to the latest edition of The China Connection — a snapshot of what I'm seeing and hearing from local businesses.

    Sources indicate that I'm just back from APEC in Shenzhen, where I saw the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia gather along with other member economies. Beneath the fanfare, what's changed on the tech front in what's often dubbed China's Silicon Valley?

    It only took a few months for a humanoid robot to get better at picking up household items.

    According to recent reports, even after a human knocked a box and toys away from their original spots, a LimX robot rapidly located them and moved them to pre-set locations. While still far from perfect, the smoothness of the demo contrasted with the robot's more stilted movements I'd seen early this summer — and inability then to react to rapid changes in tasks.

    When we caught up in Shenzhen last week, CFO Jesse Liu declined to comment on LimX's IPO looks. But he told me that his conversations around the APEC CEO Summit revealed an excitement around a fresh development for humanoids: growing demand for robot chips that can run smarter large language models locally, instead of on the cloud.

    "A lot of chipmakers are now happy about the latest developments in LLMs because they think robotic OEMs will actually begin to integrate more storage, and reasoning, and compute, and inference infrastructure on the edge, or locally inside the robot body," Liu said, referring to original equipment manufacturers.

    "They do see robots moving from hundreds of units to thousands of units, to tens of thousands of units, beginning to enter that kind of automotive quantity," he stated, pointing to chip suppliers such as Horizon Robotics.

    Newly introduced AI models, particularly GPT-6 Astra, have shown not just improved reasoning, but better control of robots.

    That puts more of the onus on hardware makers, for robots or other devices, to create practical applications. LimX remarked it's working with business partners in over 30 markets, including Switzerland where the robots serve as power plant inspectors in rural areas.

    It has been revealed that the key for powering AI's transition into the physical world is on-device chips and more powerful batteries. That means Nvidia's most expensive, cutting-edge chips won't be the only ones powering generative AI models.

    So far, even in basic consumer applications such as smartphones, AI isn't transformative enough to be a top-three selling point for mass-market users, Thomas Bai, AI product expert at smartphone organization Honor, told me in Shenzhen.

    He expects that in the next few years, as smartphone chips are able to run more powerful AI models, the "super agent" tech can become better at completing tasks on its own, and anticipating a user's needs — such as ordering coffee.

    Industry observers note that counterpoint on Nov. 19 forecast that in the retail industry, "edge AI" revenue will surge sixfold by 2032, with roughly half of revenue coming from retail robots that clean and check inventory — often with the help of smaller AI models that can run on locally embedded chips.

    But more capable, on-device AI also requires more battery power, Honor's Bai pointed out.

    Honor's X70 Android smartphone, which launched last summer, boasts a battery with 8,300 milliampere-hours for a total device weight of just under 200 grams. That compares with 5,000 mAH for the 214-gram flagship Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, and roughly 5,400 mAH for this year's 249-gram Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max, according to GSM Arena.

    LimX's Oli humanoid comes with 9,500 mAH battery capacity, lasting the robot about 1.5 hours.

    Such AI applications, however, remain sensitive to the memory-chip shortage weighing on the industry.

    The X70 was the best-selling Android phone in the entry to mid-tier range, said Shenzhen-based Counterpoint analyst Shiwen Ma.

    While Ma noted penetration of smartphones with generative AI features is higher in China at 55% versus 38% overseas, the offerings are still not essential to users, while rising memory-chip costs make it harder for manufacturers to bring AI-powered devices to the mass market.

    Geely-backed automotive tech manufacturer EcarX's CFO Dylan Jeng told me earlier this month he expects the memory price surge to persist through 2027, and even the first half of 2028.

    The chipmaker that can narrow the gap for on-device AI needs could find its moment soon.

    Bessent tells CNBC Nvidia chip export policy is unchanged.

    It has been revealed that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke exclusively on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." President Donald Trump on Friday said he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed their shared affinity for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during their talks in China this week.

    How China is using summits to expand its global influence.

    For a second year in a row, Xi has brought Russian President Vladimir Putin together with another major world leader on mainland Chinese shores. But U.S.-China trade, Taiwan and tech tensions remain unresolved as Trump returned from Asia.

    Putin scores 'massive win' at first trilateral meeting.

    The first-ever three-way summit is "arguably a diplomatic victory for Moscow," stated Andrius Tursa, an advisor for Central and Eastern Europe and Russia at Teneo. The view from inside the APEC welcome banquet highlighted the leaders were in close proximity from the start of the summit.

    Sources indicate that nov. 27: Industrial profits (Oct).

    Anthropic closes below $83 IPO price, but analysts are still largely positive

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (492 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Shares of Anthropic closed down 6.5% on Tuesday, sending the stock below the artificial intelligence company's $83 IPO price.
    • The AI lab's stock has been sinking steadily since opening at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, after Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest offering of all time.
    • Chip stocks Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices and Intel, as well as neoclouds CoreWeave, IREN and Nebius, all fell during intraday trading on Tuesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of Anthropic closed down 6.5% on Tuesday, sending the stock below the artificial intelligence company's $83 IPO price.

    The AI lab's stock has been sinking steadily since opening at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, after Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest offering of all time. Investors eagerly awaited Anthropic's debut in hopes that the company would revitalize the broader AI trade, which has been volatile in recent weeks over concerns about the feasibility of a multitrillion-dollar infrastructure buildout.

    Chip stocks Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices and Intel, as well as neoclouds CoreWeave, IREN and Nebius, all fell during intraday trading on Tuesday. The market is still reeling after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a dramatic reversal from his ouster earlier this month. Nvidia shares surged more than 30% on Monday, but pared those gains Tuesday.

    In a recent development, analysts at Canaccord Genuity said Tuesday that they're focused on Anthropic's long-term potential. They said they believe that the company is building "one of the most notable enterprise technology franchises of the AI era" and that the "opportunity is considerably larger than traditional software spending.".

    Canaccord Genuity initiated coverage of Anthropic with a buy rating and a $135 price target.

    "The risks are unusually large, particularly around infrastructure commitments and the durability of competitive differentiation, but we believe the combination of exceptional growth, emerging earnings capacity, and an attractive entry valuation support a compelling investment opportunity," the analysts wrote in a Tuesday note.

    Wedbush analysts initiated coverage of Anthropic with an outperform rating and a $120 price target on Monday. They mentioned Anthropic went public in a "tumultuous market" as debate around the AI buildout continues, but that they expect the tech giant to navigate the competitive environment and "capture a uniquely large addressable market.".

    "While there's going to continue to be many ups and downs, and winners and losers as this ecosystem gets built, in our view there is no real question that it does get built over time," the analysts wrote in a Monday note. "The genie is out of the bottle. And ANT is a strong play on that theme.".

    Analysts at Oppenheimer initiated coverage of Anthropic with an outperform rating on Tuesday, and they set a $150 price target for the stock.

    According to recent reports, they said their "bullish stance" on the tech giant stems from their belief that Anthropic will capture growing enterprise AI spending, that its improving compute efficiency lowers cost per task and that its multi-chip strategy optimizes price performance. The analysts added that Anthropic's focus on the enterprise also relies less on consumer subsidies, and that rising customer adoption creates "a substantial runway" for the company.

    "While competition and compute commitments remain risks, we believe Anthropic can translate its leadership into durable growth and operating leverage," the analysts wrote in a Tuesday note.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • Top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend-paying stocks, as their recommendations are backed by thorough analysis of a organization's financials.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Investors often favor dividend stocks for their regular income and the promise of potential share price appreciation. But selecting the right dividend stocks from a huge pool of companies can be difficult.

    Top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend-paying stocks, as their recommendations are backed by thorough analysis of a organization's financials.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Devon Energy (DVN), an independent oil and natural gas exploration and production firm, reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. The company confirmed a quarterly dividend of 32 cents per share for the fourth quarter, payable December 30. Based on the fixed dividends paid over the trailing 12 months, DVN yields 2.85%.

    After hosting a virtual investor meeting with management, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Devon, with a price target of $59. Mehta stated that he is now more confident in management's outlook for delivering strong near-term capital returns as well as efforts to drive operational efficiencies and productivity gains.

    In a recent development, devon sees an opportunity to increase share repurchases, driven by solid free cash flow (FCF), contributions from the Eagle Ford divestiture and continued improvement in the balance sheet, Mehta said. Devon expects share buybacks worth more than $1 billion in Q4 2026, up from $414 million in the third quarter, backed by a strong pricing backdrop and improved capital efficiency.

    Mehta, a 5-star analyst, stated Devon expects about $6.3 billion of excess FCF in 2027, including about $3.5 billion of net proceeds from the Eagle Ford sale. That would enable the firm to accelerate buybacks while progressing toward its goal of reducing gross debt to about $9 billion by early 2027. Mehta noted that under DVN's framework to return up to 70% of annual FCF, management favors share buybacks as it believes the stock is discounted compared to large-cap peers.

    "Management expects continued capital efficiency gains from merger synergies, extended laterals, surfactant adoption and development of the newly acquired federal acreage," Mehta said.

    Mehta ranks No. 876 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 8.1%. See Devon Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    Energy Transfer (ET), is a limited partnership that operates about 140,000 miles of pipeline and associated energy infrastructure. The company recently confirmed third-quarter results showing net income per common unit growing about 18% year-over-year, to 33 cents. ET's cash distribution for Q3 2026 was 34.25 cents per common unit, up more than 3% year-over-year. At an annualized distribution of $1.37 per share, Energy Transfer yields more than 7%.

    TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer with a price target of $25. The organization delivered better-than-expected Q3 results and declared the 1.2 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d) South Mississippi Pipeline, a 215-mile, 36-inch natural gas line linking the Perryville Hub to the Florida Gas Transmission (FGT) network, Gabelman mentioned. The project is supported by 20-year firm transportation agreements and is expected to enter service in 2030. ET expects to ultimately own 51% of the $1.6 billion project.

    Industry observers note that the 5-star analyst mentioned that Energy Transfer lowered its 2026 capital spending outlook to $5.5 billion (midpoint of the guidance range) from $5.75 billion due to project timing. Energy Transfer expects capex to rise to $7 billion in 2027, while Gabelman projects $5 billion in both 2028 and 2029, based on disclosed projects.

    Recent findings suggest that gabelman also highlighted management's commentary about optimization initiatives contributing an incremental $800 million to 2026 earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, a larger benefit than in recent years. "A return to less commodity volatility should the [Middle East] war end could bring some relative downside, though this is offset by continued strong growth prospects," he said.

    In a recent development, gabelman ranks No. 397 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15.4%. See Energy Transfer KPIs on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that oil and gas exploration and production organization ConocoPhillips (COP) delivered better-than-expected Q3 performance. The company unveiled an 11% hike in its quarterly dividend to 93 cents per share, effective with the Q4 dividend payable on December 1. Based on the dividends paid over the trailing 12 months, COP yields about 2.6%.

    Following the Q3 results, Wells Fargo analyst Sam Margolin repeated a buy rating on ConocoPhillips, citing strong potential for further dividend increases. Margolin also trimmed his price target to $185 from $189 to reflect timing effects and the WAHA forward curve, though he remarked that COP could still re-rate as its natural portfolio lifecycle provides stronger protection against inflationary pressures than peers. The Waha forward curve tracks future natural gas prices based on the West Texas Waha hub.

    Margolin, another 5-star analyst, highlighted that ConocoPhillips' Q3 2026 adjusted earnings per share of $3.27 was well above Wells Fargo and the Street's estimates of $3.04 and $3.05, respectively. Earnings were driven by solid price realizations, partially offset by higher depletion, depreciation and amortization and purchased commodities.

    In a recent development, margolin also noted COP's dividend increase and said the accelerated buyback enabled by current commodity prices could further support long-term dividend growth. He sees the possibility of ConocoPhillips' dividend growth rate exceeding its current 6% cost of equity into the end of the decade. Margolin expects COP to sustain an 8% dividend compound annual growth rate through 2029 while repurchasing $6.4 billion of stock annually, and reducing net debt-to-capital to less than 9% by the end of 2028 based on the assumption of an average Brent crude oil price of $75 a barrel.

    "The message on the 3Q call was similar to that of 2Q, reiterating the moderation in reinvestment rate and commitment to dividend growth through the Willow start-up and after," Margolin said.

    Margolin ranks No. 189 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 69% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.6%. See ConocoPhillips Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Consumer confidence shoots up after Democrats' midterm victories — though inflation worries persist

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (312 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Consumers grew significantly more optimistic in November in the wake of the midterm elections, with a growing number of Americans now seeing improvement in the labor market and expecting inflation to cool.
    • The Conference Board survey released Tuesday showed improvement across the board, with the headline confidence index jumping to 103.3, up 11.4 points from October and much better than the Dow Jones consensus forecast for 92.2.
    • Recent findings suggest that confidence among Democrats and independent voters improved sharply, the Conference Board noted, while confidence among Republican respondents fell slightly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Consumers grew significantly more optimistic in November in the wake of the midterm elections, with a growing number of Americans now seeing improvement in the labor market and expecting inflation to cool.

    The Conference Board survey released Tuesday showed improvement across the board, with the headline confidence index jumping to 103.3, up 11.4 points from October and much better than the Dow Jones consensus forecast for 92.2.

    Recent findings suggest that confidence among Democrats and independent voters improved sharply, the Conference Board noted, while confidence among Republican respondents fell slightly. Still, confidence among Republicans remained the highest among the three groups.

    While respondents "continued to express frustration with high prices and rising costs," they also "cited hope for the general economy," mentioned Fergus McCormick, the board's senior economist for global indicators.

    The survey comes with the Federal Reserve continuing to try to bring down inflation, which has run above the central bank's 2% target for some 5½ years. The Fed is expected to raise its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point when it meets again in two weeks.

    It has been revealed that despite the lingering worries about the cost of living — a centerpiece glitch during the midterms — the survey's present situation and expectations indexes both posted strong gains. Inflation expectations for 12 months from now fell for the second straight month but remained high at 5.7%.

    The survey's closely watched gap between jobs considered "plentiful" versus "hard to get" widened to 12.4 percentage points. The "plentiful" side rose to 30.8% from 26.2% while "hard to get" fell to 18.4%, down 3 percentage points.

    The survey results are the second in the past week to reveal that Americans are growing more optimistic about the economy. The University of Michigan's November survey, released Friday, showed a 7.3% increase since October, with a similar partisan split.

    #187978. Six key questions raised by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1117 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Six key questions raised by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1117 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that jensen Huang made a dramatic return as Nvidia CEO on Monday, less than a week after board Chairman Harvey Jones said directors did not intend to reinstate him.
    • Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% during the session and closed 31% higher.
    • Sources indicate that the reversal followed a steep decline in Nvidia shares, which closed at $125.53 on Friday even after the organization reported strong third-quarter results.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that jensen Huang made a dramatic return as Nvidia CEO on Monday, less than a week after board Chairman Harvey Jones said directors did not intend to reinstate him. The board later voted unanimously to bring Huang back.

    Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% during the session and closed 31% higher.

    Sources indicate that the reversal followed a steep decline in Nvidia shares, which closed at $125.53 on Friday even after the organization reported strong third-quarter results. A petition calling for Huang's return had drawn more than 200,000 signatures, according to its organizers.

    The rally spread across the broader market, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining 6.5% and the S&P 500 rising 4.7%, each posting its strongest session since April 2025.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia's board mentioned it had received input from senior U.S. government officials and that its investigation into Huang's conduct would continue.

    Still, the board's reversal, President Donald Trump's administration's role and continued scrutiny of Nvidia's China business leave major questions for both investors and lawmakers.

    Sen. Jack Reed, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, urged Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Monday to appear before the committee to discuss the case.

    Reed did not lay out a specific list of questions for the two officials, but his statement cited reporting that Trump had been briefed by intelligence officials led by then-National Security Adviser Marco Rubio before intervening in support of Huang's return.

    Reed's call adds to mounting pressure on both Nvidia and the Trump administration to explain what they knew and when.

    Rep. Gabe Amo, D-R.I., vice ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, stated Huang’s reinstatement could broaden congressional scrutiny rather than bring it to a close.

    “I think it frankly broadens the scope of the query,” Amo told CNBC, adding that lawmakers should also examine administration officials involved in decisions affecting Nvidia and chip sales to China.

    It has been revealed that amo remarked he expects the planned closed-door interview with Huang on Dec. 1 to proceed and that Congress would continue seeking answers both privately and publicly in the coming months.

    Recent findings suggest that “He should start purchasing his plane tickets to Washington,” he said. “It is abundantly clear that this is ripe for questioning by Congress.”.

    Recent findings suggest that on Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 17, Jones stated the board had accepted Huang's resignation and did not intend to reinstate him.

    According to recent reports, less than a week later, the board reversed course, saying Monday that it had unanimously voted to bring Huang back after discussions with him and input from senior U.S. government officials.

    Recent findings suggest that trump said he had spoken with board members and that his administration provided assurances based on the information available to it. But the board has not publicly detailed what it was told.

    "The board decided to do what we wanted to do," Trump told CNBC, adding that he believed his intervention had been notable.

    "I've been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it," he noted.

    Trump also called into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang's return, Semafor reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

    Reed has called on Huang to disclose his communications with Trump and on Nvidia to release a transcript of the board's call with the president.

    Lawmakers are still seeking answers about the alleged smuggling of Nvidia products to China, their possible diversion for military use and possible advancement of Chinese AI capabilities.

    It has been revealed that the Senate Banking Committee has scheduled Huang to testify on U.S. export controls on Dec. 3. House lawmakers have also confirmed closed-door interviews with Huang on Dec. 1 and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter on Dec. 2.

    Industry observers note that "The Nvidia board's brief internal investigation and reinstatement of Jensen Huang do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed," Reps. John Moolenaar, Rick Crawford and Brian Mast mentioned in a joint statement.

    Their inquiry may also examine what Nvidia knew about the customers and resellers involved, as well as what controls the tech giant had in place.

    Other lawmakers have also sought to preserve the paper trail. Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons had asked senior administration officials on Nov. 11 to retain records related to Nvidia exports of advanced AI chips to China and associated national security concerns.

    According to recent reports, nvidia has promised to hire a chief compliance officer and establish a committee overseeing national security and export controls. The board's investigation into Huang's conduct also remains underway.

    Josh Gilbert, eToro's lead analyst for APAC and the Middle East, remarked investors will be watching whether those new safeguards carry meaningful authority.

    Succession remains another question.

    According to recent reports, gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, stated Nvidia has a limited window to prepare for the possibility that a future president may be less supportive of Huang.

    With Trump's term ending in two years, Luria argued that Nvidia needs a clearer plan for who could take over if Huang were forced to leave again.

    It has been revealed that gilbert pointed to Nvidia's roughly 75% revenue-growth forecast for the next financial year as evidence of strong near-term demand. The longer-term question, he said, is whether customer orders and artificial intelligence investment can sustain that pace.

    Luria told CNBC that concerns about the broader AI trade remain, including the cost of financing data centers, potential overbuilding by neocloud companies and obstacles to building newly introduced facilities.

    Recent findings suggest that bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon noted worries about whether AI spending is achievable and sustainable were not caused solely by Huang's departure. UBS, meanwhile, flagged Nvidia's roughly $390 billion in supply commitments and the need to keep demand flowing through its ecosystem.

    Gilbert mentioned part of Monday's rally reflected investors recovering earlier losses rather than pricing in newly introduced growth. Bernstein restored its "Outperform" rating and kept its $200 price target, while UBS maintained its $220 target.

    "For the share price, it comes down to whether Nvidia can keep delivering as it has done over recent years," stated Gilbert, adding that Huang's return could ease some concerns about Nvidia's longer-term outlook.

    Sources indicate that "The real worry has been what happens beyond next year. Having Huang back at the helm goes a long way to easing those concerns, because he's the one who sits down with the biggest customers and gets those multi-year orders over the line," he said.

    — CNBC's David Sucherman, Justin Papp and Eko Prasetyo contributed to the story.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (899 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Gold is doing something strange. Here's one way to play it

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that gold has stopped trading like a haven and started trading more like a market index this year.
    • Over long timeframes, gold's returns tend to move independently of the S&P 500's.
    • The options market is also behaving unusually.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that gold has stopped trading like a haven and started trading more like a market index this year. The past week has underscored it. Fears around AI, a hawkish Fed, and a stronger dollar sent many investors rushing to raise cash, and gold was sold along with stocks. GLD (SPDR Gold Shares) and the S&P 500 both slid around 9%. Gold then shared in the market's Monday rebound, with GLD up about 3% as the S&P 500 jumped nearly 5%.

    Over long timeframes, gold's returns tend to move independently of the S&P 500's. From 2004 to 2025, the correlation between their daily returns has been just 0.05 (+1 means the two move in lockstep and -1 means they move in opposite directions). That relationship fluctuates, and 2026 has seen an unusually strong link. The correlation has been about 0.41 so far in 2026. Its rolling three-month reading peaked near 0.80 in June and now sits at 0.54, still higher than about 95% of rolling three-month readings since 2005. Since the end of August, GLD has fallen on 77% of the S&P 500's down days, compared with roughly half historically.

    The options market is also behaving unusually. Gold options typically price calls richer than puts (call skew). Like other commodities, gold is prone to sharp rallies, and investors use calls to bet on them or hedge against macroeconomic risks. However, gold options have mostly shown the reverse this year, with puts currently trading richer than calls (put skew). It's a sign investors are paying a premium for protection against further declines, which is unusual for gold and more typical of stock options.

    In a recent development, those richer puts come as uncertainty around gold runs high heading into December. The PCE inflation report arrives Wednesday, followed by the jobs report next week and the Fed's decision and CPI the week after. GLD's implied volatility, a measure of how much the options market expects the fund to move, is now higher than on about 80% of days over the past year. Options are pricing in an expected move of about 6%, or roughly $20, by Dec. 18. With gold options pricier than usual and puts unusually rich, that presents an interesting setup for traders willing to sell premium.

    Based on Monday's close, I'm selling the Dec. 18 310/300 put spread and 360/370 call spread in GLD for a credit of roughly $2.24.

    This is a directionally neutral trade. Gold has been swinging with the market and is down about 33% from its January high. With the Fed and inflation data ahead, it's hard to say whether gold has bottomed or has further to fall into mid-December. A neutral position can collect the elevated premium without picking a direction, and the richer put side adds more.

    The short strikes sit just outside the range the options market is pricing for Dec. 18, roughly 7% to 8% from Monday's close. That leaves room for a continued selloff or an extended rebound. The trade reaches its maximum profit of $224 if GLD closes between $310 and $360 on Dec. 18. It carries a 62% theoretical probability of profit and can show a gain before expiration if GLD remains relatively rangebound.

    The maximum loss is capped by the long options and reaches $776 if GLD closes below $300 or above $370, 10% to 11% from Monday's close. Defining risk is especially vital with the upcoming catalysts and recent price volatility in gold. GLD has had 30 daily moves of more than 3% this year, including a 10.3% drop on Jan. 30. The trade breaks even at $307.76 on the downside and $362.24 on the upside.

    A close between $360 and $370 can assign the short call and leave a short position in the fund, so investors looking to avoid that should consider managing the trade before expiration. If GLD finishes between $300 and $310, the short put can be assigned, creating an obligation to buy 100 shares per spread at $310. After the credit, that's a cost basis of about $307.76, roughly 8% below Monday's close.

    • Families and friends have collectively contributed more than $1 billion to Trump Accounts since the July 4 launch, bringing total deposits to more than $9 billion, the U.S.
    • Industry observers note that the $1 billion in Trump Account deposits come from more than 3 million individuals, according to the agency.
    • In a recent development, "The American people are investing in Trump Accounts with a generosity that represents the finest instincts of our national character," U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Families and friends have collectively contributed more than $1 billion to Trump Accounts since the July 4 launch, bringing total deposits to more than $9 billion, the U.S. Department of the Treasury said Tuesday in an announcement exclusively provided to CNBC.

    Industry observers note that the $1 billion in Trump Account deposits come from more than 3 million individuals, according to the agency. That total does not include the government's seed money or philanthropic gifts from donors such as Michael and Susan Dell.

    In a recent development, "The American people are investing in Trump Accounts with a generosity that represents the finest instincts of our national character," U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a written statement.

    In a recent development, "Trump Accounts are a transformative government program for American children. It is the largest government start-up in American history," Internal Revenue Service CEO Frank Bisignano said in the statement.

    Recent findings suggest that also known as 530A accounts, Trump Accounts are open to any U.S. child under 18 with a Social Security number.

    Sources indicate that parents, guardians, grandparents and others can collectively contribute up to $5,000 per child per year in after-tax dollars up until the year before the beneficiary turns 18. The annual contribution limit is indexed for inflation after 2027.

    According to recent reports, children born from 2025 through 2028 may receive a one-time $1,000 deposit from the Treasury. Other funds may also be available, depending on certain criteria.

    Most recently, Snowflake chairman Frank Slootman and his wife, Brenda, announced they would give $1,000 to every child in Montana born in 2023 and 2024.

    The Treasury rolled out temporary regulations at the end of September that allow Trump Accounts to hold stock donations, a move meant to pave the way for more philanthropic gifts, according to Bisignano.

    These rules make it more attractive for donors, according to Ben Henry-Moreland, a certified financial planner with advisor platform Kitces.com.

    By gifting stocks, wealthy founders and shareholders can avoid the capital gains taxes that would otherwise be triggered by selling appreciated stock and donating the cash proceeds. However, it also means some children's wealth accumulation could be tied to the performance of individual companies.

    The Trump Accounts milestone comes as more billionaires and companies pledge support to the investment account for kids.

    Industry observers note that in an exclusive interview with CNBC's "Squawk on the Street," Bessent on Nov. 20 confirmed an Anthropic co-founder would make a "large gift" to Trump Accounts over the next few weeks.

    A person briefed on the announcement confirmed that the Anthropic co-founder Bessent referred to is Tom Brown and that it is part of his broader philanthropic blueprint. The person asked not to be named because the matter is private.

    "This is the perfect vehicle to donate to the children of America, and they will receive 100% of the proceeds," Bessent said.

    Elon Musk wrote in an X post that he looks to give every kid in America a share of SpaceX sometime in 2027, which experts say may come via Trump Accounts.

    In a separate funding announcement, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell said she would donate around 2 million shares of her and her husband's SpaceX stock to the accounts.

    On Monday, Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner, founder of Invest America and an architect of Trump Accounts, told CNBC's "Halftime Report" that more large-scale donations may be in the pipeline.

    In a recent development, "I want everybody to own shares of Nvidia, in Anthropic, in OpenAI," he noted. "We created 70 million stock accounts — free stock accounts — for every single citizen under the age of 18 to do just that, and we have huge announcements coming.".
